chapters.title: 1  Sarko's Awakening
chapters.summary: Sarko remembers freezing during a flood in his old village. His awakening calls him toward a courage he does not yet believe he has.
chapters.text: Chapter One: Sarko’s Awakening Sarko had spent most of his old life feeling invisible. Back in his rain-soaked village, other young lions were praised for bravery, strength, and confidence while Sarko faded quietly into the background. He remembered standing helplessly during a terrible flood years earlier, frozen while others rushed to save frightened families. Nobody blamed him afterward—but he blamed himself every day since. Deep inside, he feared that when people truly needed him, he would fail them again. Rain hammered the rooftops of Sarko’s old village the night everything changed. The memory still clung to him. For most of his life, Sarko had believed he was ordinary—forgettable even. Far away in the peaceful forest kingdom of Chadash Adamah, a young lion named Sarko opened his eyes in a strange new room. Everything around him felt dreamlike—but deep inside, he knew this was real. The last thing Sarko remembered was falling asleep during a terrible storm back in his old village. Then suddenly… he woke up here. “Where am I?” Sarko whispered. The room was beautiful. Wooden walls were covered with glowing vines and shining flowers. Above the doorway, carved carefully into the wood, was one word: Sarko. “My name…” he murmured. Sarko slowly climbed out of bed. The moment his paws touched the floor, he froze. Beside the wall stood a giant set of shining armor made of bright white metal trimmed in gold. A glowing dove symbol was carved into every piece. And the armor looked huge. Way too huge for the little lion cub he remembered being. Sarko looked down at himself—and gasped. His body had changed. Instead of being small and skinny, he was now tall, strong, and full of energy. His golden fur shimmered softly in the light, and his muscles felt powerful. His hearing was sharper too—he could hear birds chirping far outside the room. “This is amazing…” Near the corner stood a tall mirror covered in sparkling crystals. Sarko stepped closer and stared at his reflection. That’s when he noticed it. A glowing dove mark shined softly on his forehead and right paw. The marks didn’t feel scary. They felt warm. Safe. Peaceful. Sarko smiled a little. “Maybe this place isn’t so bad after all.” He turned back toward the armor. “Well,” he chuckled nervously, “might as well try it on.” The armor fit perfectly—almost like it had been made just for him. He placed on the shining breastplate, leg plates, sturdy sandals, golden belt, and finally picked up a huge shield almost bigger than he was. The shield didn’t feel like just a tool. It felt important. Special. Sarko looked in the mirror again. Now he truly looked like a hero. Then suddenly— Knock. Knock. Knock. Sarko jumped. “Uh… come in?” The door opened slowly. Standing outside was a cheerful gray wolf wearing twin swords across his back. His bright blue eyes sparkled with excitement. “Hello!” the wolf said happily. “My name is Waiz!” Before Sarko could answer, Waiz grabbed his paw and shook it enthusiastically. “I’m Sarko,” the lion replied carefully. Waiz grinned. “You probably have a LOT of questions.” Sarko laughed awkwardly. “You could say that.” Waiz stepped into the room. “This world is called Chadash Adamah,” he explained. “The New Earth. Animals from many lands come here to begin incredible adventures.” Sarko listened closely. “In this world, miracles, spirit, and strength work together,” Waiz continued. “There are brave heroes, mysterious creatures… and dangerous monsters too.” Sarko’s ears perked up. “Dangerous monsters?” Waiz nodded. “But you’ve been given something rare. You’re a Child of God.” Sarko blinked. “…Is that good?” Waiz laughed. “For a beginner? SUPER good! You’ve got a strong start!” He stepped closer, his tone softening again. “And it also means you have a purpose.” Sarko straightened. “A purpose?” Waiz nodded. “You know…” he said quietly, glancing at the glowing dove mark on Sarko’s forehead, “that mark means Heaven is calling you.” Sarko blinked. “Heaven?” Waiz nodded. “Come here.” The gray wolf motioned for Sarko to follow him. Curious, Sarko walked beside him toward the doorway. Waiz pulled the door open wider, revealing the glowing streets of Chadash Adamah stretching below. Animals moved through the city carrying lanterns, supplies, and shining weapons. In the distance, forests rolled across the horizon beneath towering mountains. Then Waiz pointed far beyond them. Sarko’s breath caught. A brilliant golden light filled the distant sky. It looked almost like the sun. But brighter. Softer. Alive. “That,” Waiz said quietly, “is the Heavenly City.” Sarko stared in awe. “It’s beautiful…” “It’s the City of God,” Waiz continued. “The place where perfect light lives. No fear. No corruption. No death. Every Child of God journeys toward it.” Sarko looked down at his glowing mark. “So… I’m supposed to go there?” Waiz smiled. “Yes.” Then his tone became more serious. “But listen carefully, Sarko… nobody reaches the Heavenly City alone.” Sarko tilted his head. “What do you mean?” Waiz leaned lightly against the doorway. “That City wasn’t made for pride. It was made for unity. Every Child of God is given gifts, strengths, and abilities—but no one is given everything.” He pointed gently toward Sarko’s shield. “A Shepherd protects.” Then toward his own twin swords. “An Evangelist guides and encourages.” Waiz spread his paws slightly. “Others defend. Others scout. Others lead. Others see danger before it comes. Alone, every warrior has weaknesses.” He looked directly at Sarko. “But together?” A grin spread across his muzzle. “We survive what would destroy us alone.” Sarko listened carefully. “So… I need a team?” Waiz laughed gently. “Oh, you absolutely need a team.” Then his voice lowered. “And your team will need you too.” That surprised Sarko. “Me?” Waiz nodded firmly. “Your light isn’t meant to shine for yourself alone. A Shepherd keeps others standing when they’re wounded. When they’re afraid. When they feel like giving up.” The wolf looked back toward the radiant City. “No one reaches the City by proving they’re the strongest.” The distant golden light reflected in his blue eyes. “We reach it by learning to love, trust, protect, forgive… and walk together.” Quiet settled over the doorway. Then Sarko looked again toward the endless horizon. The journey suddenly felt bigger than just him. Somehow… That made him feel less afraid. “I think I understand,” Sarko said gently. Waiz grinned. “Good.” Then he pointed dramatically toward the glowing City. “Because trust me—if you try surviving this world alone…” He paused for effect. “…you’re gonna get eaten.” Sarko burst out laughing. Waiz laughed too. Then Sarko looked back down at the glowing mark on his paw. “It feels… alive.” “It is,” Waiz said. “But it’s something you have to guard. Not just with strength—but with your choices. If you turn toward evil… the light can fade.” Sarko swallowed. “…Can it go out?” Waiz met his eyes. “Yes.” Quiet returned briefly. “And if it does… you can’t enter the City.” Sarko looked back toward the Heavenly City shining beyond the horizon. Then slowly nodded. “I won’t let it go out.” Waiz smiled warmly. “I believe you.” Sarko’s tail flicked with curiosity. “What kind of hero am I?” Waiz crossed his arms proudly. “You’re a Shepherd class. You protect others and heal them. Your ability is called Miraculous Heal.” “And you?” Sarko asked. Waiz grinned wider. “I’m an Evangelist class. I guide, encourage, and help others understand their path.” Sarko’s eyes lit up. “That’s awesome.” Waiz chuckled. “It keeps me busy.” He turned slightly toward the door. “I actually have to go soon,” he said. “There are others who need guidance.” Sarko’s ears dipped slightly. “Oh…” Waiz smiled reassuringly. “But I’ll catch up with you soon.” That seemed to lift Sarko’s spirits. “Really?” “Of course,” Waiz said. “For now, explore. This world has a way of answering questions… when you’re ready for them.” Sarko nodded. “Okay… I can do that.” Waiz nodded approvingly. “Our team leader is a Tiger named Levi,” he added. “And we train under Diago, a wise bear. You’ll meet them soon enough.” Sarko grinned. “I hope so.” Then, with a friendly flick of his tail, the wolf stepped out into the glowing street. “I’ll see you soon, Sarko!” The door gently closed. Sarko stood still for a moment. Everything still felt new. Different. But deep inside… For the very first time in his life— He felt like he belonged. And now… He had a purpose. Not just to explore this world— But to walk toward the light.

chapters.title: 2  The Town of First Light
chapters.summary: In First Light, he discovers a town of animal people, radiant gifts, and a place where his new journey can begin.
chapters.text: Chapter Two: The Town of First Light Sarko didn’t waste any time; he quickly gathered some supplies, opened his front door and stepped outside. The moment he did, the world opened before him. Golden sunlight poured across streets of smooth stone. Buildings rose high with carved wooden beams, bright white walls, and rooftops that shimmered softly like bronze beneath the sky. Colorful banners hung from windows, each marked with symbols Sarko did not yet understand. And everywhere he looked, animals moved with purpose. Some had glowing markings. Some had horns. Some walked on two legs, others on four. A graceful silver-feathered crane passed by, carrying baskets filled with glowing fruit. Nearby, a massive stone-furred gorilla hammered glowing metal at a forge, sparks flying like tiny stars. A group of young fox and rabbit cubs raced through the street laughing, chased by a floating orb that buzzed and chirped angrily at them. Sarko stood frozen. “Okay…” he whispered. “Definitely not my old world.” Still wearing his shining armor, the dove mark glowing softly against his fur, Sarko began to walk deeper into the town—remembering Waiz’s words: “For now, explore. This world has a way of answering questions… when you’re ready for them.” As he moved forward, heads began to turn. Some animals smiled warmly at him. Some lowered their heads respectfully. Others noticed the glowing dove marks on his armor— —and quickly stepped aside. That made Sarko uneasy. Back in his old life, he had felt invisible most of the time. Now… everyone was looking at him like he mattered. Even though he hadn’t done anything yet. The feeling sat strangely in his chest. Soon, the streets opened into a massive marketplace. Wooden stalls filled the square, overflowing with all kinds of items—shining weapons, polished armor, fresh food, bubbling potions, ancient scrolls, and strange crystals humming with quiet energy. A voice called out to him. “New arrival!” Sarko turned. A short, round badger with a thick, braided beard waved him over, his eyes twinkling with excitement. “I can always tell,” the badger said cheerfully. “Wide eyes. Stiff walk. Completely overwhelmed.” Sarko blinked. “That obvious?” “Painfully.” The badger chuckled and pointed at Sarko’s shield. “Shepherd class, eh? Rare. Very rare.” Sarko glanced down. “I’m still trying to figure out what that means.” The badger leaned closer, lowering his voice. “It means… when everything goes wrong…” “…everyone will look at you.” Sarko swallowed. “That sounds… stressful.” “It is,” the badger said with a grin. “But also glorious.” Before Sarko could reply, a soft chime echoed inside his mind. A glowing screen suddenly appeared in front of his eyes. STATUS WINDOW UNLOCKED Name: Sarko Race: Child of God Class: Shepherd Level: Role: Support Tank Primary Gift: Miraculous Heal Current Skills: • Shield Guard • Minor Restoration • Radiant Mark • Miraculous Heal Sarko stared at it. “Oh… There are stats?” The badger burst out laughing. “Of course there are! How else would the world measure growth?” Then his expression shifted. “Well now…” Sarko looked up. “What?” “For level one…” the badger said slowly, “…those are very unusual.” Sarko smiled slightly. “Waiz said I had a strong start.” The badger shook his head. “For level one,” he corrected. “Do not confuse potential… with victory.” The words hit harder than Sarko expected. He nodded gently. Waiz’s voice echoed again in his mind: Not just strength… your choices. A quiet shift passed through the marketplace. Conversations softened. Movement slowed. Sarko turned. At the far end of the street stood a towering grizzly bear. His fur was dark, streaked with silver, and across his back rested a massive two-handed sword—its blade thick, worn, and powerful, like it had seen countless battles. Beside him stood Waiz, the gray wolf, waving both paws excitedly. “Sarko!” Waiz shouted. “Found you!” Sarko’s face lit up. Waiz jogged over, slightly out of breath but grinning. “Told you I’d catch up,” he said. The bear didn’t wave. He didn’t smile. He just watched Sarko… Like a weapon being tested. Waiz gestured proudly. “This is Diago.” The great bear stepped forward. Each step felt heavy—like the ground itself respected him. Diago’s presence felt immovable. Like a mountain that had stood through too many storms. “I am Diago,” he said, his deep voice steady. “Teacher class.” Sarko straightened instinctively. “Yes, sir.” Diago’s eyes moved slowly—taking in the armor, the shield, the glowing mark. “You are a Shepherd, Good.” He rested one massive paw near the hilt of his greatsword. “Then as your teacher…” He stepped closer, his presence unshakable— “…let’s find out if you can survive being one and follow me.” With that they began to leave the city through the eastern gate.

chapters.title: 3  The Mentor of Iron
chapters.summary: Diago takes Sarko beyond the eastern gate. Hard training teaches him to stand under pressure with his shield.
chapters.text: Chapter Three: The Mentor of Iron The eastern gate closed behind them with a deep, echoing groan. Outside the town walls, everything changed. The warmth and beauty of the marketplace faded into rugged wilderness. Jagged hills stretched toward distant mountains, while enormous trees twisted across the land like ancient giants frozen in time. Strange birds circled high overhead, their sharp cries echoing through the valley. Sarko adjusted the massive shield. “So… where exactly are we going?” Diago, the towering grizzly bear, answered without turning around. “To see whether you die under pressure.” Waiz, the gray wolf, laughed nervously. “He means training.” Diago glanced sideways. “I meant exactly what I said.” Sarko wasn’t sure how he felt about that. They followed a winding dirt path until they reached a massive circular field surrounded by towering stone pillars. The ground was torn with deep claw marks, gouges, and craters from countless battles. Weapons racks lined the edges. Training grounds. Diago stepped into the center. “This world rewards growth,” the great bear said. “But growth does not come from comfort. It comes from pressure. Pain. Fear. Sacrifice.” He pointed one massive claw toward Sarko. “Your class makes you valuable. Valuable creatures become targets.” Sarko nodded gently. Diago continued. “You are not a striker. You are not a hunter. Your purpose… is survival.” He stepped closer, his presence heavy and unshakable. “If your pack lives… you win.” The words hit Sarko differently than expected. Back in his old life, strength meant standing above others. Here… Strength meant protecting them. Without warning, Diago tossed a wooden training sword across the field. “Fight me.” Sarko barely caught it. “Wait—right now?!” “Yes.” “I’ve been here for like… two hours.” Diago unsheathed his heavy training blade. “And enemies will politely wait for you to adjust?” “…Fair point.” Waiz quickly backed away, tail flicking as he moved to the edge of the field. “Oh this is gonna hurt.” Sarko raised the wooden sword awkwardly in his paw. Diago studied him. “Terrible stance.” “I’ve never used a sword before.” “I know.” Diago moved. Fast. Too fast. Sarko barely saw the strike before pain exploded across his side. THUD. He crashed into the dirt, the breath knocked from his lungs. Waiz winced. “Oof.” Sarko groaned. “What WAS that?!” Diago stood calmly in the center of the field. “A lesson.” Sarko forced himself back to his feet. Every instinct told him to run. But something deeper refused. He raised the sword again. Diago attacked instantly. This time, Sarko lifted his shield on instinct. CRACK. The impact shook through his entire body—but he stayed standing. Diago’s eyebrow lifted slightly. “Better.” Then the real assault began. Strike after strike hammered against Sarko’s defenses. Diago attacked from every angle with brutal precision, forcing Sarko backward across the arena. Again. Again. Again. Every mistake was punished. Time blurred. Sarko’s muscles burned beneath his armor. His legs trembled. His breathing grew heavy. But slowly… He adapted. The shield began to feel lighter. The sword felt less foreign. And little by little… He began to read Diago’s movements. It happened. Diago swung low. Sarko blocked. Countered. And for the first time— His blade struck Diago’s armor. CLACK. The field fell silent. Waiz blinked. “No way…” Diago looked down at the mark on his armor. Then, slowly… He smiled. The first real expression Sarko had seen from him. “Again,” Diago said. The next few days were relentless. Morning until night, Diago pushed Sarko beyond exhaustion. Shield drills. Sword forms. Defensive positioning. Spiritual resistance training. Endurance runs through forests filled with hostile beasts. Meditation exercises that forced Sarko to confront fear, anger, doubt—and memories from his old life. Each night, he collapsed from exhaustion. Each morning, he woke stronger. Then came the monsters. Diago led Sarko and Waiz into a narrow canyon crawling with creatures called Hollow Wretches— Twisted, corrupted animals. Their bodies were stretched and unnatural—like broken wolves, deer, and apes fused with shadow. Their limbs were too long, their movements jerky and wrong. Their eyes glowed deep red with emptiness. Level 5. Weak alone. Deadly together. “Perfect training opponents,” Diago said. Sarko stared. “There’s like… thirty of them.” “Yes.” “That’s not comforting.” “Good.” The creatures shrieked— —and charged. Waiz drew both swords instantly, fur bristling with excitement. “Showtime!” The battle exploded. Waiz moved like lightning through the swarm, blades flashing as Wretches fell apart around him. Sarko raised his shield just as one slammed into him. The force pushed him backward. Another struck from the side. Then another. Panic surged. Too many— “Sarko!” Diago’s voice thundered. “Focus!” Sarko planted his paws. Breathe. Think. Protect. The glowing dove mark on his paw ignited. Warm, radiant energy surged through him. A new instinct awakened. Without thinking, Sarko slammed his shield into the ground. “Shield Guard!” Golden light burst outward. A powerful barrier formed around him and Waiz just as multiple Wretches slammed into it. They recoiled, screeching. Waiz’s eyes widened. “Okay—THAT was awesome!” Sarko stared at his shield. He had done that. A Wretch leapt toward Waiz from behind. Sarko reacted instantly. “Minor Restoration!” Light burst from his paw, wrapping around Waiz, healing his wounds instantly. Waiz laughed mid-fight. “I could get used to this!” Something settled deeper inside Sarko. The fear didn’t disappear. But something stronger rose above it. Purpose. He understood now. His power wasn’t meant to destroy. It was meant to protect. To preserve. Somehow… That felt greater. Hours later, the final Wretch collapsed. Nobody celebrated. Waiz collapsed backward. Sarko just tried to breathe. Quiet settled over the canyon. A chime echoed in Sarko’s mind. LEVEL UP New Skill Unlocked: • Fortress Aura Sarko blinked. “Wait… level five already?!” Waiz grinned. “Quick learner.” Diago crossed his massive arms. “No.” Sarko looked at him. Diago’s eyes remained fixed on the battlefield. “He learns… because he fights for others.” For the first time since arriving in this world— Sarko truly believed… He might survive it.

chapters.title: 4  Synergy
chapters.summary: Sarko and Waiz face fear together. Their gifts grow stronger when they trust one another rather than fight alone.
chapters.text: Chapter Four: Synergy That night, nobody trained. Waiz threw pebbles into the rain while Sarko adjusted shield straps for the third time. “You do that when you’re nervous,” Waiz said. Sarko looked down. “I do?” “Yep. Also when you’re scared.” Silence lingered. “I’m scared a lot,” Sarko admitted. Waiz smiled faintly. “Good.” Sarko blinked. “If you stop being scared completely,” Waiz said quietly, “you stop caring what happens to people.” Rain poured across the training grounds. Cold wind howled between the stone pillars as Sarko stood in the center of the arena, breathing heavily beneath his armor. Water ran down his golden fur, dripping from the edges of his shield. Weeks had passed since he arrived in Chadash Adamah. And everything was changing. Fast. His movements were sharper now. His reactions quicker. The massive shield no longer felt heavy—it felt natural. Like part of him. Across from him stood Diago, the towering grizzly bear, and Waiz, the swift gray wolf. Both were bruised. Mostly because Diago believed “learning through suffering builds character.” Waiz called it abuse. Diago called it Tuesday. “Again,” Diago ordered. Waiz groaned, shaking water from his fur. “We’ve been training since sunrise!” “And you’re still alive,” Diago replied calmly. “Meaning I’m being too gentle.” Waiz muttered something about emotional damage. Sarko let out a small laugh— —but Diago’s expression hardened instantly. “This time,” the great bear said, pointing a heavy claw at Sarko, “you will stop thinking about your abilities one at a time.” Sarko tilted his head. “What do you mean?” Diago stepped forward into the rain. “Weak fighters use skills separately,” he said. “Strong fighters combine them.” Lightning flashed behind him. “Elite fighters create synergy.” The word hung in the stormy air. “Your class is not built for destruction,” Diago continued. “It is built for amplification.” Waiz’s ears perked up and a grin spread across his muzzle. “Ohhh… we’re finally doing combo training.” Diago gave a single nod. “Show me.” At that moment, the stone pillars surrounding the arena began glowing red. The ground trembled. From the earth rose towering training constructs—massive creatures formed of black stone and iron, shaped like corrupted animal warriors with glowing eyes. Level 18. Sarko swallowed. “There are six of them…” “There were thirty Wretches,” Diago replied. “You survived.” “Barely.” “Survival still counts.” The constructs attacked. One charged straight toward Sarko, while two flanked Waiz from either side. Waiz drew both blades instantly. “Alright, big guy!” he shouted. “Support me!” Sarko planted his paws. Think. Not separate. Together, they covered each other's weaknesses. A construct swung a massive iron fist toward Waiz. Sarko reacted. “Fortress Aura!” Golden light burst from his body. A radiant dome expanded outward, wrapping around both him and Waiz. Instantly— Waiz accelerated. His movements became lighter. Faster. The construct’s strike missed by inches. Waiz blinked mid-dodge. “Oh—that’s new!” Diago crossed his arms. “Passive enhancement field,” he muttered. Waiz spun behind the construct and slashed both blades across its legs. CLANG. The creature staggered. Another construct charged from the side. Sarko lifted his paw instinctively. “Radiant Mark!” A beam of light shot forward, marking the construct’s chest with a glowing dove symbol. Waiz’s eyes widened. “I can see its weak points!” He lunged. His blades struck directly into the mark. BOOM. The construct shattered into pieces. Sarko stared. Waiz stared. Then both shouted— “THAT WAS AWESOME!” Diago turned slightly, hiding what might have been the smallest smile. “Continue.” The remaining constructs advanced together. Sarko’s mind raced. Shield Guard blocks. Fortress Aura boosts. Radiant Mark exposes weakness. Healing sustains. Separate… limited. Together… An idea sparked. “Swords up!” Sarko called. Waiz didn’t hesitate. The moment the constructs closed in, Sarko slammed his shield into the ground. “Shield Guard!” Golden barriers erupted outward— But this time, Sarko controlled them differently. Instead of one dome… He shaped them into narrow paths. Corridors. Funnels. The constructs were forced into tight spaces. Waiz grinned. “Ohhh… you’re thinking now.” “Just move!” Waiz exploded forward like lightning. The confined constructs couldn’t surround him anymore. One by one, he tore through them while Sarko redirected attacks with precise shield movements. One construct broke through. It slammed directly into Sarko. CRASH. He flew backward, skidding through mud. Pain shot through his ribs. The construct raised its weapon for a finishing blow— Sarko grabbed the glowing mark on his chest. “Miraculous Heal!” Light erupted. But this time— Something changed. The healing energy surged outward— Into Fortress Aura. Waiz froze. His entire body ignited with golden light. Energy pulsed through him. “What did you just do?!” he shouted. “I DON’T KNOW!” Waiz vanished. Not fast— Gone. A sonic boom cracked through the arena. Sarko could barely track him. SLASH. SLASH. SLASH. Three constructs collapsed instantly. Silence followed. Rain hissed against the ground. Waiz stood still, stunned. Sarko blinked. Diago walked forward slowly. One remaining construct rose behind him— Without even turning— Diago swung one massive paw. The construct exploded. Then he looked at Sarko. “That…” Diago said carefully, “…was not normal.” Sarko stood slowly. “What happened?” Diago’s eyes narrowed. “Your Miraculous Heal amplified through Fortress Aura.” Waiz pointed dramatically. “He turned me into a missile.” Diago nodded. “Support classes capable of force multiplication are rare.” Sarko frowned. “Force multiplication?” “It means,” Diago said, “your strength is not measured by what you can do alone.” He gestured toward the destroyed battlefield. “It is measured by what your allies become… because of you.” The realization hit deeply. Back in his old life, Sarko had tried to prove his own strength. But here— His power came from lifting others. Somehow… That felt right. A soft chime echoed in his mind. SKILL EVOLUTION AVAILABLE New Traits Unlocked: • Healing Amplification • Movement Enhancement (for marked allies) • Spiritual Resistance Increase Waiz grinned wide. “Oh yeah… we are becoming terrifying.” Diago turned his gaze toward the distant mountains. Concern crossed his face. “Not yet,” he said gently. Sarko noticed immediately. “What is it?” Diago remained silent for a moment. Then finally: “The stronger your light becomes…” He looked directly at Sarko. “…the more darkness will notice you.”

chapters.title: 5  The Gathering of Light
chapters.summary: The team gathers as darkness notices their growing light. First Light becomes a home worth protecting.
chapters.text: Chapter Five: The Gathering of Light Night had fallen by the time they returned to town. Lanterns glowed along the streets of First Light, their warm amber light reflecting off rain-soaked stone. Music drifted from nearby dens while merchants packed away their goods beneath the silver moon. But Diago, the great grizzly bear, was unusually quiet. Sarko noticed. Ever since the training battle—since the moment his power amplified through others—his mentor’s expression had sharpened. Focused. Alert. Like he sensed something coming. The stronger your light becomes… the more darkness will notice you. Waiz, the gray wolf, was still talking. “I’m serious,” he said. “I think I moved so fast I saw the future.” “You screamed the entire time,” Diago replied. “That’s called tactical enthusiasm.” Sarko laughed. Then they arrived. At the far edge of town stood a massive stone hall overlooking the valley. White banners marked with glowing dove symbols hung along its walls. The headquarters. Waiz pushed the doors open. “Everyone! The new guy survived!” Heads turned. The first Sarko noticed was a sleek, powerful cheetah resting near the fire. Her golden coat was marked with dark spots, and her focused eyes locked onto him instantly. A long, glowing spear rested beside her. She stood with effortless precision. “That depends on your definition of survived.” Waiz pointed. “See? This is why morale suffers.” “I am Amaya,” she said. “Vanguard class.” Everything about her radiated speed, discipline… control. Near the window sat a small, glowing axolotl, her soft frills gently pulsing with light. A floating focus orb balanced near her, shifting with quiet energy. “Hailey,” she said calmly. “Ranger.” THUNK. A glowing shot struck perfectly into a beam. “…still practicing.” Waiz sighed. “Sure you are.” Across the room, a massive rhino stood. “Isaac. Shield brother!” CLANG. Sarko staggered. “I felt that in my spine…” Near the staircase stood a gentle white deer, glowing softly with a peaceful light. “I am Naomi the prophet” “I saw you long before you came.” Peace settled over Sarko. “You carry hope.” Waiz clapped. “Food. Now.” They gathered. Food. Laughter. Life. Sarko expected heroes to feel larger than life. Instead, they interrupted each other, argued about food, and complained about injuries. Only after watching them joke, argue, and help each other did Sarko notice something deeper. Every smile here seemed hard-earned. Sarko felt it fully now— A pack. Isaac told loud stories. Waiz exaggerated. Amaya corrected with sharp precision. Hailey calmly guided glowing shots through the air. Diago judged silently. Naomi watched with quiet warmth. Everything was right. Darkness. Every candle died. Waiz stood instantly. “That’s bad.” A cold pressure filled the room. Death-cold. Sarko’s mark burned. Outside— Screams. “Positions!” Diago roared. Everyone moved. BOOM. The doors exploded inward. Dark smoke poured in. And from it— A towering black panther stepped forward. His fur swallowed the light. Shadow energy crawled across his body like living darkness. A cracked silver crown rested on his head. And on his forehead— A shattered dove mark glowed. Sarko’s breath caught. “No…” The panther smiled. “You feel it… don’t you?” His voice layered unnaturally. “We share the same origin.” Waiz growled. “Name.” The panther bowed mockingly. “Malachar.” Naomi whispered: “The False Shepherd…” Even Diago tensed. Malachar’s eyes locked onto Sarko. “So… Heaven chose another.” Pressure crushed the room. “…how long before your light breaks?” He moved. SHATTER. Too fast. His blade struck— CLANG. Isaac intercepted. Shockwaves cracked the walls. “Heavy…” “And you are weak.” Darkness exploded— Isaac was launched. The battle erupted. Amaya moved first— A blur. Pure speed. Pure control. Her strikes landed in rapid, calculated bursts. Malachar dodged. Effortless. Hailey fired. Three glowing shots— Perfect angles. One grazed Malachar. He paused. “…interesting.” Waiz attacked— Caught instantly. “Still illegal.” CRASH. Down. Sarko’s heart raced. They were losing. Badly. Diago engaged— For a moment, matched him. Darkness surged. Diago was thrown. Malachar wasn’t trying. “Sarko!” Naomi called. “Not alone!” It clicked. Synergy. “EVERYONE TO ME!” They regrouped. “Sanctuary Aura!” Golden light exploded outward. Everyone strengthened. Hailey focused— “Left opening!” “MARK HIM!” “Radiant Mark!” Light struck Malachar. His smile faded. “What—” “NOW!” Diago roared. Everything aligned. Hailey fired a binding shot. Isaac slammed the ground. Amaya—gone. Impact. She struck the exact weak point with flawless precision. Waiz followed through. And Sarko— “Miraculous Heal!” Amplification. Not healing— Power surged through everyone. Light filled the hall. Hailey’s final shot ignited— Released. Amaya struck. Waiz hit. Everything connected— BOOM. The hall exploded in radiant light. Nobody moved immediately. Dust drifted through broken beams while everyone waited to see who was still standing. Nobody spoke for a while. Not because they had nothing to say. Because surviving took energy too. The team simply existed together for a few minutes—breathing, checking wounds, sharing quiet relief. Those moments mattered more than victories sometimes.

chapters.title: 6  The Apostle
chapters.summary: Malachar strikes the guild hall. The team wounds him, but his unnatural shadow heals and the battle deepens.
chapters.text: Chapter Six: The Apostle Dust and shattered stone filled the air. The explosion from Amaya’s strike had torn through the guild hall, blowing out walls and cracking pillars to their foundations. Rain poured through the broken ceiling as golden and black energy clashed violently across the battlefield. Malachar, the black panther, stumbled backward. A thin line of dark blood ran down the side of his face. Silence fell. Waiz, the gray wolf, blinked. “…we actually hit him.” Amaya, the cheetah, lowered her spear slightly, breathing hard. “Not enough.” She was right. The wound was already healing. Darkness crept across Malachar’s fur like living shadow, sealing the damage unnaturally fast. Still… Something had changed. He wasn’t amused anymore. Now— He looked cautious. And angry. Malachar’s glowing eyes locked onto Sarko. “You amplified all of them at once…” His voice dropped. “That ability should not exist at your level.” Sarko tightened his grip on his shield. “I’m starting to hear that a lot.” Suddenly— Dark energy exploded outward again. The entire hall shook. Isaac, the armored rhino, stepped forward instantly, planting himself in front of the team. “Incoming!” BOOM. The blast smashed into Sarko’s Sanctuary Aura. Cracks spread across the golden barrier. Hailey, the axolotl, narrowed her eyes. “He’s increasing output.” Waiz spun his blades. “How is he STILL getting stronger?!” Naomi, the glowing white deer, suddenly smiled. “He’s here.” The doors creaked open behind them. Heavy footsteps echoed through the ruined hall. Slow. Steady. Confident. The team relaxed instantly. Even Diago. A massive tiger stepped into the room. His long tiger tail moved calmly behind white-and-gold armor, and a deep crimson cloak flowed behind him, untouched by the rain. The dove mark on his forehead burned brighter than anyone else’s. At his side rested a sheathed sword wrapped in golden chains. The moment he entered— The entire atmosphere shifted. Not fear. Authority. Malachar’s expression darkened. “…Levi.” The tiger stopped beside Sarko. His gaze was calm. Sharp. Ancient. He looked around at the destruction. “I leave for one supply run,” he sighed, “and you nearly destroy the headquarters.” Waiz pointed immediately. “To be fair, evil panther started it.” Levi ignored him. “The False Shepherd.” Malachar’s aura flared. “And the Apostle.” Sarko glanced between them. Yeah… they definitely had history. Levi turned to Sarko. “You must be the new Shepherd.” Sarko straightened instantly. “Yes, sir.” Levi studied the glowing marks on him. Then nodded. “Good.” That one word hit harder than anything else. Malachar drew his blade. Darkness poured from it. Levi remained calm. “Formation seven.” Instantly— The team moved. Isaac and Sarko took front line. Amaya and Waiz split flanks. Hailey moved rear-center beside Naomi. Diago stayed mobile. And Levi… Walked forward alone. Sarko blinked. “That’s the plan?” Diago smirked. “You’re about to understand.” Malachar attacked. The ground shattered beneath him as he lunged. His blade crashed downward— SHING. Levi’s chained sword left its sheath. Golden light erupted. CLANG. The collision froze the battlefield. Shockwaves blasted outward. Sarko’s eyes widened. Levi hadn’t moved. Not even an inch. Malachar narrowed his eyes. Levi spoke calmly. “You rely too much on force.” Malachar unleashed a storm of attacks. Dark slashes tore through the air— But Levi blocked every strike. Perfectly. No wasted movement. No panic. Sarko whispered: “He’s reading him…” Naomi shook her head. “He’s leading him.” And then Sarko saw it. Every block shifted Malachar’s position. Every movement guided him. Like a trap. Levi suddenly called out: “NOW.” Everything exploded into motion. Isaac slammed his hammer. “EARTHBREAKER!” Stone pillars erupted around Malachar. Hailey fired glowing arrows that chained between them. “Binding Shot!” Amaya lunged— Faster than sight. “Piercing Current!” Lightning surged through the trap. Malachar roared— Darkness surged outward— But Sarko reacted instantly. “Sanctuary Aura!” Golden light expanded. Levi’s voice cut through: “Sarko—mark him!” “Radiant Mark!” Light burned onto Malachar’s chest. This time— Levi moved. Gone. A streak of gold crossed the battlefield. Malachar barely raised his blade— BOOM. Levi’s strike detonated against the mark. The hall exploded outward. Rain blasted through the ruins. The dust cleared. Malachar stood at the far end. Breathing hard. Armor cracked. Blood dripping. And for the first time— Fear flickered. Quiet settled over the room. Then Malachar laughed. Quiet. Not mocking. Impressed. “So this is your answer…” His gaze shifted to Sarko. “The new Shepherd completes your pack.” Levi lowered his blade. “You lost the moment you came alone.” Malachar smirked. “Yes.” Darkness gathered behind him. Twisting. Moving. Shapes forming. Sarko felt it instantly. More enemies. Stronger ones. Malachar stepped backward. “When we meet again…” His eyes locked onto Sarko. “I will not be alone.” The broken dove mark pulsed violently. “And when your light breaks…” His voice darkened. “…you will understand why mine did.” The shadows swallowed him. Gone. Nobody spoke immediately. Rain poured. Waiz looked around. “So…” He gestured at the destroyed hall. “…who’s cleaning this up?” Isaac pointed at Sarko immediately. “New guy.” “WHAT?!” Levi sheathed his sword. He smiled. Faint. But real. The tiger looked over the team. Bruised. Exhausted. Still standing. Together, they covered each other's weaknesses. And quietly, he said: “The Kingdom may truly have hope after all.”

chapters.title: 7  Seeds in the Rain
chapters.summary: The guild rebuilds after the storm. Amaya's discipline reveals old fear, while the party learns to keep hope alive.
chapters.text: Chapter Seven: Seeds in the Rain While repairs continued, Amaya quietly rewrapped old scars beneath her foreleg. Sarko noticed. “You hurt?” “No.” Pause. “Used to be slower,” she admitted. That surprised him. “One hesitation cost somebody safety.” Her ears lowered slightly. “So now I train until hesitation disappears.” Sarko realized discipline was not confidence. It was fear given structure. The storm finally began to calm. Rainwater dripped through the shattered remains of the guild hall while the team worked silently through the wreckage. Broken stone covered the floor. Splintered beams leaned dangerously overhead. Their home had nearly been destroyed. And yet… No one looked defeated. Isaac, the armored rhino, hauled fallen pillars aside with brute strength, snorting with effort. Waiz, the gray wolf, dragged a single wooden plank across the floor—dramatically. “This,” Waiz declared, “is oppression.” “You are carrying one board,” Amaya, the cheetah, replied flatly. “It’s emotionally heavy.” Nearby, Hailey, the axolotl, had somehow repaired half a wall— Crooked. She stared at it for a moment. “…intentional.” Then spent ten minutes pretending it was artistic design. And through it all— Levi, the tiger, stood quietly near the broken entrance, looking toward the distant mountains where Malachar had disappeared. Sarko approached him slowly. As Levi spoke about brokenness and growth, Sarko noticed sadness hidden beneath the tiger’s composure. Even the strongest leaders carried battles no one else could see. “You think he’ll come back soon?” Levi nodded once. “Yes.” Too calm. Sarko glanced back at the damaged hall. “You don’t seem angry.” Levi looked toward him. “At the destruction?” Sarko nodded. Levi stepped outside into the cool night air and motioned for him to follow. Below them, the town was alive. Animals moved together beneath lantern light—repairing homes, tending the wounded, carrying supplies. Young foxes and rabbits worked beside larger creatures without hesitation. No one had given up. Levi leaned against the stone railing. “Do you know why this world is called Chadash Adamah?” Sarko shook his head. “It means New Earth,” Levi said. “Not because it is free from suffering…” His gaze drifted toward the broken hall behind them. “…but because God is rebuilding everything.” The words stayed with Sarko. Levi knelt and picked up a small seed from the wet soil. “Life here follows a pattern.” He held the seed gently between his claws. “A seed remains alone unless it enters the ground.” He pressed it into the earth. “And before something greater can grow…” His paw covered the soil. “…the seed must first break.” Sarko watched gently. Levi stood. “Breaking hurts. But it isn’t the end.” He looked back at the town. “Tonight brought fear. Damage. Loss.” “Look again.” Sarko did. Animals helping each other everywhere. Carrying burdens. Lifting one another. No panic. No selfishness. Only unity. Levi smiled faintly. Levi looked across the damaged town. “Darkness wanted ruin.” He glanced toward the people rebuilding. “But God isn't finished.” Something stirred inside Sarko. Back in his old life, he had feared pain. Avoided it. Questioned it. But now… Maybe pain wasn’t always abandonment. Maybe it was preparation. Levi adjusted the crimson mantle resting across his shoulders. “Malachar believes brokenness leads only to corruption.” His voice hardened slightly. “That is where he fell.” Sarko looked toward the mountains. “What happened to him?” Levi was silent for a long moment. “He was once like us.” Sarko’s ears twitched. “He carried Heaven’s mark. Protected others. Led with strength.” “What changed?” Levi’s eyes darkened. “Suffering without understanding.” Rain dripped softly around them. “He saw loss. Death. Prayers unanswered.” Levi looked down. “And he decided… if pain exists, God must not be good.” A chill ran through Sarko. “But pain didn’t destroy him,” Levi said. “Hopelessness did.” Levi looked directly at him. “That is why your role matters.” “Mine?” “You are a Shepherd.” Levi pointed toward the town below. “A Shepherd does not only heal wounds.” His voice carried weight. “He reminds others why they should keep going.” It hit deeply. Healing wasn’t just physical. It was hope. Levi turned back toward the others. “Gather everyone.” Moments later, the team stood together in the damaged hall. Isaac leaned on his hammer. Waiz somehow had dirt on his face despite minimal effort. Amaya stood calm and ready. Hailey continued adjusting something that definitely wasn’t working. Naomi, the white deer, watched Levi knowingly. Levi looked at them all. When Levi stepped into battle beside them, Sarko finally understood something deeper behind the Apostle’s calm expression. Levi carried grief—and kept choosing people anyway. Then spoke: “We leave at sunrise.” Sarko blinked. “Leave?” Levi nodded. “The Heavenly City awaits.” The words shifted the air. Waiz grinned instantly. “Finally.” Isaac slammed his hammer down. “Adventure!” Hailey looked slightly nervous. Amaya closed her eyes and nodded. Naomi smiled gently at Sarko. “The journey begins now.” Levi walked toward the broken doorway as moonlight faded. “The road ahead will test you.” His voice echoed. “You will face fear. Loss. temptation.” “You will also witness miracles.” The glowing dove mark on his forehead lit the room. “And no matter how dark it becomes…” His voice steadied everything. “…God always finishes what He starts.” Outside— That night, Diago sat near the fire long after everyone else quieted. "I trained others before all of you," he said suddenly. Nobody interrupted. "Most died." The group froze. Diago stared into the flames. "Not because they were weak." His massive paws tightened. "Because I was gentle." Silence settled heavily. Sarko looked at his teacher differently after that. Diago was not harsh because he lacked compassion. He was harsh because grief had already taught him what failure costs. That evening, nobody trained. No monsters. No drills. Just firelight. Waiz lost badly at a game involving carved stones and claimed the rules were unfair. Isaac admitted he once got stuck in a doorway carrying supplies. Even Amaya laughed. Sarko mostly listened. He realized something important. Heroes became family long before they became legends. The first light of dawn rose over the horizon. Sarko looked at his team. Bruised. Tired. Still moving forward. Something stirred within him. Not fear. Not instinct. A calling. The glowing dove mark on his paw pulsed gently. Naomi, the white deer, noticed immediately. “Your ability is responding.” Sarko looked down. “It feels… different.” Levi nodded. “Then listen.” Sarko stepped into the center of the clearing. The others watched gently. He closed his eyes. He didn’t try to control it. He trusted. Warmth spread through his chest like sunlight breaking through clouds. The air around him began to glow. Waiz blinked. “Uh… are you doing that?” “I don’t know…” The energy surged. “Miraculous Heal.” Golden light flowed outward. Not violently. Gently. Like warmth wrapping around every soul present. It passed through the team. Isaac’s injuries vanished. Waiz’s bruises faded. Hailey’s exhaustion disappeared. Amaya’s tension released. And deeper still— Fear lifted. Fatigue faded. The weight of battle… gone. Waiz slowly touched his chest. “…okay that felt illegal.” Isaac flexed proudly. “Shield brother stronger!” Hailey blinked in disbelief. “My energy… fully restored…” Even Diago, the great grizzly bear, looked impressed.

chapters.title: 8  The Weight of the Journey
chapters.summary: On the road, Sarko and his friends face the weight of past failures and admit the fears they have carried.
chapters.text: Chapter Eight: The Weight of the Journey Rain tapped softly against the shelter, and for one sharp moment Sarko was back in the floodwater of his old world—watching others move while he stood frozen. He tightened his paws around the edge of his shield. He had become stronger since then, but a quiet fear still followed him: if someone was hurt while he was there, maybe it meant he had failed again. The team sat quietly around the fire. Isaac volunteered for first watch. Again. “You always take watch,” Naomi said. Isaac stared into the darkness. “Last time I didn’t... people disappeared.” Nobody joked after that. Not even Waiz. Waiz opened his mouth for a joke. Nothing came out. He looked away. “I don’t know how to laugh this one off.” Nobody mocked him. That honesty mattered more. Isaac stared deeper into the fire. “I protect because I remember names.” Sarko tilted his head. Isaac looked away. “The ones I failed.” Silence settled around the campfire. Not awkward. Heavy. Real. Amaya lowered her spear across her lap. “I hesitated once.” Her eyes stayed on the flames. “One moment.” She finally looked at the team. “Not today.” The fire crackled softly between them. For the first time, Sarko realized strength sounded different when heroes stopped pretending. These weren’t fearless warriors. They were wounded people choosing to keep protecting others anyway. Dawn broke quietly over First Light. The storm had passed, leaving the world washed clean beneath soft golden sunlight. Mist drifted through the valley while animals slowly emerged from their homes, beginning to rebuild what had been damaged. Inside the guild hall, the team prepared in silence. Weapons were sharpened. Armor was adjusted and repaired. Supplies were packed into travel satchels. But exhaustion hung heavily over them. The battle with Malachar had taken more than anyone wanted to admit. Isaac, the armored rhino, had his massive foreleg wrapped tightly from shoulder to hoof. Hailey, the axolotl, rested against a broken pillar, her glowing frills drooping slightly from exhaustion, eyes half-lidded after pushing herself too hard with her radiant archery. Waiz, the gray wolf, was covered in bruises despite insisting— “I’m totally fine.” Amaya, the cheetah, didn’t even look at him. Nobody believed him. Sarko, the lion, stood near the entrance, tightening the straps on his shield when he noticed Levi watching the team gently. Not critically. Not worried. Thoughtful. Then Levi spoke. “Do you remember how all of you were standing at the end of the battle?” Waiz groaned. “Barely.” Isaac lifted his head proudly. “Victory stance.” “You were unconscious against a wall,” Amaya replied. “Spiritually standing.” A faint smile touched Levi’s muzzle. Then his expression sharpened. “You were exhausted because each of you gave everything you had.” His golden eyes moved across the room. “No one here could have survived Malachar alone.” Because it was true. Even Diago, the great grizzly bear, said nothing. “And yet together…” Levi’s gaze rested on Sarko. “…you forced one of the most dangerous enemies in this world to retreat.” Sarko looked down slightly. It still didn’t feel real. Levi stepped into the center of the hall. “Many believe the purpose of the journey is reaching the destination.” He shook his head. “But Heaven does not only care about where you arrive…” His voice softened. “It cares about who you become.” The room stilled. Levi gestured toward the cracked walls. “Yesterday, each of you faced fear.” He looked at Waiz. “You learned courage is not the absence of fear…” Then at Hailey. “…but moving forward despite it.” He turned to Isaac. “You learned strength is not domination…” Then to Amaya. “…but discipline under pressure.” Finally— He looked at Sarko. “And you learned that true power is not standing above others…” The dove marks on Sarko’s fur glowed gently. “…but lifting them higher.” It hit deeply. Because in his old life… Sarko had chased outcomes. Success. Approval. Arrival. Believing that once he reached something greater, he would finally feel complete. But here— The moments shaping him most weren’t victories. They were struggles. Lessons. People. Levi moved toward the doorway as sunlight poured in. “God could bring us there immediately if He wanted.” Sarko blinked. “Then why doesn’t He?” Levi smiled faintly. “Because growth takes time.” He shrugged slightly. “None of us would survive becoming who we need to be overnight.” Outside, birds soared across the morning sky. “A blade is strengthened through fire.” “A tree is rooted through storms.” “A traveler grows through the journey.” Levi adjusted the crimson mantle resting across his shoulders. “And love becomes real when it chooses to remain through difficulty.” Silence followed. Not heavy. Peaceful. The kind that settles truth deep inside. Naomi, the white deer, spoke gently. “The journey itself is part of the gift.” Levi nodded. “Yes.” Then he looked at Sarko. “You once wondered why you were brought here.” Sarko straightened. “Not just to reach the Heavenly City.” Levi gestured to the team. “But to become the kind of person who can live there.” Those words burned into Sarko’s heart. Because suddenly— Everything made sense. The pain. The training. The battles. The uncertainty. None of it was wasted. God wasn’t just leading them somewhere. He was shaping them along the way. Waiz suddenly stretched dramatically. “Well,” he said, “I’m emotionally inspired now.” Amaya rolled her eyes slightly. “That lasted longer than usual.” Isaac lifted his hammer with a grin. “Journey time.” Hailey stood carefully, balancing a few floating tools and arrows. “They are probably stable.” Sarko blinked. “Probably?” “Very confident maybe.” Diago grabbed his pack. “Move.” That night, Naomi sat beside Sarko gently. "You still carry the storm," she said gently. Sarko froze. "The flood?" Naomi nodded. "May I show you something?" Her mark glowed gently. Light spread between them. Rain. Darkness. His old village. His younger self sitting alone where nobody could see. Then Sarko noticed something else. Light. Standing beside him through every fearful moment. During the loneliness. During the prayers. During the nights he thought nobody heard. His breathing shook. "He was there..." Naomi smiled. "Always." The vision shifted. The Heavenly City. His team. His mark. His purpose. "You thought Heaven ignored you." Her voice stayed gentle. "But Heaven was preparing an answer." Sarko wiped his eyes. "Why show me this?" Naomi looked toward the stars. "Because Shepherds remind others they are not alone." She looked back at him. "Sometimes Shepherds need reminding too." The team gathered near the broken entrance. Sarko studied them gently. Different personalities. Different wounds. Still walking together. That morning, Sarko watched his team carefully. For the first time in his life, he understood what real family looked like. Sunlight stretched across the valley. Far in the distance— Beyond forests, mountains, and unknown dangers— A radiant glow shimmered on the horizon. The Heavenly City ahead of them. Sarko stared at it gently. Still far. Still unreachable—for now. But something inside him had changed. The destination wasn’t the only miracle. Becoming was too. Levi stepped forward. And together— The team began their journey toward the light.

chapters.title: 9  The Hidden Garden
chapters.summary: After helping a farming settlement, the party enters the Hidden Garden, where protection means caring for ordinary lives too.
chapters.text: Chapter Nine: The Hidden Garden The team spent half a day helping a damaged farming settlement rebuild fences and repair homes. No battles came. Only tired families. Sarko used Miraculous Heal on sore muscles. Hailey repaired water systems. Naomi encouraged frightened children. For once, they protected ordinary life instead of saving the world. The road beyond First Light stretched endlessly ahead. Rolling hills gave way to towering forests, and ancient stone paths wound through valleys untouched by civilization. Massive trees arched overhead like cathedral pillars, while sunlight filtered through their leaves in shimmering beams. The team traveled carefully. Not because they feared the wilderness— But because the wilderness watched back. Naomi suddenly stopped walking. Her glow brightened gently. "Not left," she said gently. Isaac blinked. "Road go left." "Not today." Levi studied her expression. "Vision?" Naomi nodded once. The team changed course. Seconds later— BOOOOOOM. Massive stone pillars collapsed exactly where they would have walked. Waiz slowly pointed at Naomi. "Okay. Prophet deer picks directions now." Sarko, the young lion, noticed it constantly now. Movement between trees. Faint glowing eyes deep within the shadows. Creatures observing in silence. This world was alive in a way Earth had never been. After several hours, exhaustion still clung to the group. Isaac, the armored rhino, limped heavily. Waiz, the gray wolf, pretended his ribs weren’t injured—despite wheezing every few steps. Hailey, the axolotl, looked like she might collapse from the sky if she kept fighting. Even Amaya, the cheetah, held her spear with the slightest tremble. Levi, the tiger, noticed everything. Of course he did. He raised one paw. “We rest here.” They stopped beside a quiet stream. Crystal-clear water flowed over smooth stones. Soft blue flowers lined the banks, glowing faintly in the light. For the first time since leaving First Light— Peace settled. The stream began to glow. Everyone turned. The water shimmered brighter— Until the entire clearing filled with radiant light. Sarko raised his shield— Levi gently lowered it. “Wait.” The water parted. And from within it— A being stepped forward. An angel. Its form radiated power—tall, wrapped in flowing garments of light that moved like liquid gold. Vast glowing frills extended behind it, not made of feathers, but of pure radiant energy. Its presence filled the clearing with overwhelming peace— And undeniable authority. The forest fell silent. No wind. No sound. Even the leaves seemed to hold still. Waiz whispered: “…that’s definitely an angel.” Sarko felt his knees weaken. Not from fear— From awe. Every creature present felt it. The instinct to bow. Only Levi remained standing, lowering his head respectfully. The angel’s glowing gaze settled on Sarko. “Bearer of restoration.” Its voice echoed like music layered over thunder. Sarko lowered his head slightly. “You carry the light of renewal.” Each word felt alive. True. The angel extended a radiant hand toward the forest beyond the stream. “There is little time.” The trees shifted. A hidden path revealed itself where nothing had stood before. Naomi’s eyes widened. “The Hidden Garden…” Levi’s voice lowered. “I thought it was legend.” The angel looked over the team. “Those who walk in unity may receive what lies within.” Its gaze sharpened. “But only those who remain as one.” The path began to glow. The angel dissolved into radiant light. Its radiant form became streams of gold— Its presence faded— And it was gone. Nobody spoke immediately. Waiz pointed immediately. “Well obviously we’re going in there.” “No argument,” Hailey said quickly. Diago crossed his arms. “This could be a trap.” Levi shook his head. “No.” His eyes remained fixed forward. “This is an invitation.” They crossed the stream. Entered the hidden path. And everything changed. The deeper they walked, the more the forest transformed. Glowing flowers lit their steps. Ancient ruins rested between massive roots. The air hummed with spiritual energy strong enough to make Sarko’s fur stand on end. Finally— The path opened. Everyone stopped. At the center stood a massive tree of silver light. Its roots stretched across the clearing. Golden fruit hung from glowing branches. And floating before it— Seven radiant crystalline shards. Levi stepped forward slowly. “…Evolution Shards.” Hailey nearly lost his balance. “Those are REAL?!” Amaya’s calm composure cracked slightly. “These were lost centuries ago…” Waiz pointed excitedly. “What do they do?” Levi answered carefully. “They awaken the deeper potential within your abilities.” Sarko blinked. “…they evolve our power?” Levi nodded. “Yes.” The tree pulsed. Light surged. One shard floated toward each of them. Sarko reached out. The moment he touched it— The world vanished. Light consumed everything. Visions flooded his mind. Battles. Cities. People crying out. Souls restored. Armies protected by radiant shields. And at the center— A Shepherd. Standing against overwhelming darkness. Light pouring endlessly from his paws. The angel’s voice echoed within him: “Protection without sacrifice is weakness.” “Healing without truth is temporary.” “But love poured out becomes unbreakable.” The shard dissolved into Sarko’s chest. Power surged violently. The dove marks ignited brighter than ever before. SKILL EVOLUTION COMPLETE New Abilities: • Shared Burden • Light of Renewal • Guardian’s Covenant Sarko staggered back. The others transformed as well. Waiz’s blades ignited with radiant wind. Amaya’s spear crackled with lightning. Isaac’s armor expanded with glowing runes. Hailey’s arrows multiplied into orbiting constellations. Naomi’s light deepened. Levi watched silently. Proud. The silver tree dimmed. The air shifted. Diago’s voice dropped. “We’re not alone.” Darkness moved between the trees. Multiple presences. Watching. Sarko felt it instantly. The power had drawn them. Far beyond the forest— A familiar voice whispered through the shadows. “So…” Malachar. “…the Kingdom’s champions are awakening.”

chapters.title: 10  Fractures
chapters.summary: Malachar brings coordinated shadow warriors into the Garden. Their unity tests the bonds of Sarko's own team.
chapters.text: Chapter Ten: Fractures Malachar’s eyes moved past Sarko. Toward Levi. “You taught me protection,” he said gently. Levi remained still. “You told me sacrifice had meaning.” Darkness gathered. “Then I watched people die anyway.” For once— Sarko saw grief beneath Malachar’s anger. The Hidden Garden darkened. Moments earlier it had felt holy. Peaceful. Now tension spread through the forest like poison. Shadows moved between the glowing trees. One by one, figures stepped out from the darkness beside Malachar—the black panther. And instantly— Everyone felt it. These weren’t ordinary enemies. They moved with purpose. Coordination. Unity. Malachar stepped forward slowly, his shadow-covered fur reflecting the silver light of the ancient tree. This time— He was smiling. “You’ve grown quickly,” he said calmly. His eyes scanned the radiant energy surrounding Levi’s team. “Faster than I expected.” Sarko, the lion, tightened his grip on his shield. Then he saw them. At Malachar’s side stood a massive gorilla, wrapped in chains of black iron. A cracked metal mask covered his face, and a colossal greataxe rested on his shoulder. Raw power. Beside him— A sleek black pantheress, her form shifting like smoke. Crimson eyes glowed as spectral blades floated around her like fangs. An assassin. Further back— A thin, pale serpent, coiled upright, gripping a twisted staff made of bone and crystal. Dark symbols floated around it endlessly. A corrupted mage. And finally— A young lion, wearing shattered white armor marked with a broken dove symbol. Sarko’s chest tightened. Another fallen Child of God. Levi, the tiger, stepped forward slightly. “You brought Shepherds into corruption.” Malachar’s smile faded. “No.” He glanced at the fallen lion beside him. “They chose truth after Heaven abandoned them.” The corrupted lion stared coldly at Sarko. “You still believe suffering has purpose?” His voice carried deep bitterness. “You’ll learn.” Levi’s eyes sharpened. “No,” he said firmly. “You forgot.” Darkness exploded outward. The battle began. The chained gorilla charged first. The ground shattered beneath him as he swung the massive axe toward Isaac, the rhino. BOOM. Isaac barely blocked. The impact launched him across the clearing. He slammed into a glowing tree, cracking it. Waiz’s eyes widened. “He hits harder than Levi!” “Focus!” Amaya, the cheetah, snapped. The shadow pantheress vanished instantly. Too fast— SLASH. Blood cut across Waiz’s shoulder. “OW!” Another strike hit Hailey, the axolotl, mid-flight. The serpent mage raised its staff. “Grave Dominion.” Dark energy flooded the battlefield. The ground blackened. The air thickened. Everything slowed. Heavier. Harder. Sarko realized instantly— They were fighting a team. Just like them. Darkness surrounded Sarko. Too many enemies. Then Naomi shouted: "Shield high—NOW!" Instinct moved before thought. CRASH. A devastating strike slammed into Sarko's raised shield. Naomi exhaled gently. "Sometimes God shows moments before they happen." She smiled gently. "Sometimes moments matter." Malachar walked calmly through the chaos toward Sarko. “You feel it now, don’t you?” Dark energy pulsed around him. “The world is not divided by good and evil.” His broken mark burned. “It is divided by those who survive suffering…” His eyes locked onto Sarko. “…and those destroyed by it.” Sarko reacted. “Kingdom Sanctuary!” Golden light erupted outward. The pressure lifted. Waiz regained speed. Amaya’s lightning reignited. Hailey’s orbiting constellations expanded. Levi called out: “Formation!” The team moved instantly. Now— Their evolved abilities flowed together. Naturally. Isaac slammed his hammer down. “Fortress Dominion!” Golden stone erupted from the earth, dividing the battlefield. Amaya launched forward. “Storm Piercer!” Lightning crashed down toward the serpent mage. Hailey raised both glowing frills. “Celestial Convergence!” Her multiple arrows fused into one big energy arrow— BOOM. The forest lit with light. And Sarko— Sarko felt it. Connection. Unity. Not separate. Together, they covered each other's weaknesses. He raised both paws. “Shared Burden!” Golden threads linked the team instantly. Pain shared. Strength balanced. Energy unified. Waiz blinked mid-fight. “WAIT—that’s insane.” Isaac laughed. “WE ALL TANK NOW!” They pushed forward. The serpent mage faltered under Hailey’s assault. Amaya broke through the assassin’s shadows. Isaac matched the gorilla’s strength. And Levi— Drove Malachar backward with relentless precision. Hope surged. They were winning. Malachar smiled. Not worried. Planned. “Tell me, Shepherd…” Dark energy pulsed outward. “How long before one of them falls… because of you?” Sarko froze. The words hit. Hard. Malachar pointed. At Waiz. “He hides fear behind laughter.” At Hailey. “She doubts herself.” At Amaya. “She carries guilt in silence.” At Levi. “And your Apostle…” Malachar’s voice darkened. “He blames himself for every soul he cannot save.” The team hesitated. Just for a moment. But it was enough. The assassin struck. SLASH. Amaya cried out as blades cut into her side. Isaac turned— The gorilla smashed him. CRASH. He dropped. Hailey panicked. Her focus had turned to distraction. BOOM. The blast knocked Waiz and Diago off balance. The formation broke. Instantly— The enemy surged forward. Malachar’s voice echoed. “Yes…” Darkness expanded. “This is how corruption begins.” Sarko’s heart pounded. The golden threads flickered. Their unity— Breaking. Malachar pointed his blade at him. For the first time, Sarko understood. Malachar wasn't striking armor. He was striking places people tried to hide. Malachar’s words cut deeply because they were true. Every member of the team carried fractures they tried to hide. “You lift others well.” His smile turned cold. “But division…” The broken mark flared violently. “…destroys them faster than any blade.” Levi blocked another strike— But Sarko saw it now. Even Levi was struggling. Because the battle had changed. It wasn’t just physical anymore. It was spiritual. And their greatest strength— Unity— Was beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: 11  Strength Through Surrender
chapters.summary: As the formation breaks, Sarko learns that a Shepherd can protect others without trying to control every outcome.
chapters.text: Chapter Eleven: Strength Through Surrender Sarko had spent so much of the journey trying to become strong enough to keep everyone safe. But surrender was teaching him something harder: a Shepherd could be faithful without controlling every outcome. He could protect. He could strengthen. He could stand beside others. But he could not take God’s place in their lives. The battlefield descended into chaos. The Hidden Garden shook beneath explosions of light and shadow as Levi’s formation began to break apart. Isaac, the armored rhino, forced himself back to his hooves, blood running down his face. Amaya, the cheetah, knelt low, one paw pressed tightly against her wounded side. Hailey, the axolotl, balanced unevenly, breathing fast, her glowing frills trembling after her overextended barrage. Waiz, the gray wolf, moved recklessly now—frustration overtaking his precision. And at the center— The golden threads of Sarko’s Shared Burden flickered weaker and weaker. Malachar, the black panther, saw it instantly. His smile widened. “Yes…” Dark energy surged around him like a storm. “Now you understand.” His broken dove mark burned violently. “Unity built on strength alone cannot survive pressure.” Levi, the tiger, blocked another crushing strike, claws digging into the earth. Malachar leaned closer. “Eventually…” Their blades locked. “…everyone breaks.” BOOM. The impact forced Levi backward for the first time. Sarko’s heart tightened. Fear spread again. Not fear of losing— Fear of failing each other. Somehow… That hurt more. Waiz shouted. “This is my fault!” The battlefield stilled for a moment. Waiz winced as another spectral blade cut across his arm—but he didn’t laugh. Didn’t deflect it. He looked at the others. “I lost focus first.” He swallowed. “I joke because… I hate feeling weak.” The golden threads steadied slightly. Amaya lowered into a fighting stance. “I judged all of you for mistakes I make myself.” Her voice was calm. Honest. “I carry pressure like pride… instead of trust.” The light strengthened. Hailey trembled mid-air. “I’m afraid of failing all of you.” Her voice shook. “So I force things. I pretend I’m in control… when I’m not.” Her orbiting energy stabilized. Isaac stood fully again, gripping his hammer. “I thought strength meant carrying everything alone.” He looked at Sarko. “But shield brother shares burden.” Then at the others. “So should I.” The threads brightened. Malachar’s expression faltered slightly. “No…” Naomi, the white deer, stepped forward gently. “Pride isolates.” Soft golden light flowed from her. “But humility reconnects.” Sarko felt it. Understanding. The enemy’s strength came from domination. Control. Isolation. But theirs— Came from surrender. Trust. Grace. Levi smiled. Not because they were winning— Because they were learning. He planted his blade into the ground. “Listen!” Golden light erupted from him. “Pride demands perfection before belonging.” His voice thundered. “But the Kingdom was never built that way.” The team turned toward him. “God does not unite perfect souls.” The dove mark on his forehead blazed. “He unites surrendered ones.” Something inside Sarko broke open. Not pain— Freedom. He realized he had still been trying to prove himself. Trying to earn his place. Trying to become worthy. But none of them stood together because they were perfect. They stood together because they needed each other. And that— Made them stronger. Malachar roared. “ENOUGH!” Darkness exploded outward violently. “You call weakness strength?!” Levi stepped forward calmly. “No.” Their eyes locked. “We call dependence wisdom.” The battlefield shifted. The golden threads transformed. No longer flickering— Now blazing. Every member of the team became connected through radiant streams of light. Chosen. Sarko felt everything. Their fear. Their strength. Their trust. And instead of weakening him— It multiplied him. A chime echoed through his soul. KINGDOM SANCTUARY EVOLUTION New Traits Unlocked: • Unity Amplification • Grace-Bound Resonance • Burdens Shared Become Burdens Lifted Golden energy surged across the battlefield. Malachar’s team staggered. “What is this?!” the serpent mage hissed. Waiz grinned. “Ohhh we’re back.” This time— They fought as one. The shadow assassin lunged— Isaac intercepted instantly. The chained gorilla struck— Hailey redirected the impact mid-jump. Amaya created openings— Waiz flowed through them effortlessly. Naomi’s foresight aligned perfectly with Levi’s commands. And Sarko— Stood at the center. A living heartbeat connecting them all. Every movement synchronized. Every action strengthened. Because now— They weren’t pretending to be strong. They were choosing to stand together in weakness. And that made them unbreakable. Malachar’s forces began to fall back. The assassin stumbled. The mage lost control. The chained gorilla was driven backward. And finally— Levi reached Malachar. CLANG. Their blades collided. Golden light burst between them. Malachar strained. “You think humility makes you righteous?!” Levi stood firm. “No.” He pushed forward. “Grace does.” BOOM. Malachar was thrown backward, crashing into the roots of the silver tree. He looked shaken. Not physically. Spiritually. His gaze moved across the team. Connected. Trusting. Fighting for one another. And something flickered in his eyes. Something buried. Something lost. Sarko saw it. Beneath the anger— Malachar looked alone. The black panther rose slowly. Darkness still swirling around him— But quieter now. “You still believe…” he said lowly, “…that souls remain loyal after enough suffering?” Levi lowered his blade slightly. “Yes.” Malachar looked away. “…No.” But this time— He didn’t sound certain. Behind him, the shadows shifted again. Not retreating. Not attacking. Watching. Waiting. The tension in the garden remained. Unresolved. Heavy. Like something greater had only just begun. And Sarko realized— This battle wasn’t the end. It was only the fracture.

chapters.title: 12  The Dragon King
chapters.summary: Rex Draconum arrives. He calls dependence weakness, while Levi answers that love remains when strength fails.
chapters.text: Chapter Twelve: The Dragon King Rex looked across the wounded team. Not with hatred. Disappointment. “You still believe dependence protects people,” he said calmly. His eyes settled on Isaac’s injuries. “Strength would have prevented this.” Levi answered immediately. “No.” The tiger stepped forward. “Love stayed when strength failed.” The Hidden Garden fell into silence. Not peaceful silence. Warning silence. The kind that comes when something greater than the battle itself begins to arrive. Malachar, the wounded black panther, stood beneath the glowing silver roots. Darkness twisted around his body in unstable waves. Yet— He was smiling. Slowly. Almost… reverently. Levi, the tiger, noticed immediately. And for the first time since the battle began— Concern crossed his expression. Not fear. But close. Malachar wiped dark blood from his muzzle. “You still don’t understand, Levi.” His broken dove mark pulsed violently. “You think I fell because I hated God…” The shadows behind him deepened unnaturally. “…but I fell because I met something stronger than my pain.” Sarko, the lion, felt his chest tighten. The forest trembled. Trees bent away as if the world itself feared what approached. Naomi, the white deer, whispered: “No…” Isaac, the rhino, gripped his hammer. “What coming?” The sky darkened. Not clouds. Wings. A massive shadow passed overhead, blotting out the light. Pressure followed instantly. Crushing. Ancient. Predatory. Sarko dropped to one knee, gasping as the force pressed down like an ocean. Only Levi remained standing. The trees shattered as something descended. A dragon. A massive black dragon, scales like obsidian armor, glowing with crimson fractures beneath its surface. Its horns curved like a crown of war. Its eyes— Ancient. Commanding. Unforgiving. The ground shook as it landed. And upon its back stood a towering white tiger. His fur was pale as snow, striped with faint silver that shimmered under the dim light. Dark royal armor wrapped around his powerful frame, and a flowing crimson mantle rested across one shoulder like a banner of conquest. His presence was calm. Controlled. Absolute. Malachar bowed immediately. “My king.” Levi stepped forward slowly. Rex Draconum did not feel like an ordinary enemy. He felt like the embodiment of absolute control—a king who had convinced himself that dependence and vulnerability only led to suffering. Even his calmness felt dangerous. “…Rex Draconum.” The name itself carried weight. Waiz whispered: “That’s… your king?” Levi’s voice hardened. “That is the Dragon King.” Rex Draconum did not feel like an ordinary enemy. He felt like the embodiment of absolute control—a king who had convinced himself that dependence and vulnerability only led to suffering. Even his calmness felt dangerous. Rex Draconum’s golden eyes drifted across the team. Not with rage. With judgment. They settled on Sarko. Interesting. The word echoed directly into Sarko’s mind. Felt. Not heard. Rex stepped down from the dragon’s back, each movement measured. Sarko understood one thing immediately. This wasn't someone trying to look powerful. This was someone who trusted power more than people. Sarko understood immediately why others feared him. Rex radiated control—not because he trusted strength, but because he trusted nothing else. “You carry light… unusually well.” His voice was smooth. Refined. Dangerous. Levi tightened his grip. “Why reveal yourself now?” Rex tilted his head slightly. “Because hope grows dangerous when ignored.” He raised one clawed paw. “Allow me to correct expectations.” CRACK. The air split. Sarko’s Kingdom Sanctuary shattered instantly. Not weakened— Destroyed. The team dropped under overwhelming pressure. Waiz coughed blood. Isaac couldn’t lift his hammer. Amaya strained just to stand. Naomi trembled. “He’s suppressing everything…” Levi stood. Barely. Rex looked around. “This is restraint.” Fear spread. Because this wasn’t an attack. This was control. Rex moved. Gone. Reappeared. CRASH. Levi was launched through multiple massive trees. “LEVI!” Sarko roared. The Apostle rose again— But blood marked his muzzle. The team froze. They had never seen him overpowered. Rex looked… unimpressed. “You’ve grown slower.” Levi stood firm. “And you’ve grown emptier.” Rex lifted his paw again. Crimson energy gathered. Levi shouted: “DO NOT—” Too late. Isaac stepped forward. “Shield wall!” BOOM. The blast struck. Isaac was launched deep into the forest. Gone from sight. The shockwave shattered the garden. Sarko stared. That wasn’t effort either. Rex lowered his paw calmly. “You see now.” His voice echoed. “There are levels your unity cannot yet reach.” Malachar stood beside him again. And Sarko understood. Why he fell. Because this— Felt impossible. Rex turned back to Sarko. Curious. Not angry. “Tell me, Shepherd…” His gaze pierced deeply. “When those you protect begin to fall…” Malachar’s pain flickered beside him. “…will your faith endure what his did not?” Sarko couldn’t answer. Because for the first time— He felt the weight of that question. Rex smiled faintly. “As expected.” He turned away. “We leave.” Malachar hesitated. “My king… we can finish them.” Rex didn’t look back. “No.” His gaze shifted slightly toward Levi. “They are not ready.” The black dragon spread its glowing frills. Rex leapt onto its back with effortless grace. Darkness gathered around Malachar and the others. But before leaving— Rex spoke once more: “The Heavenly City will not remove suffering.” His voice thundered. “It will reveal whether your faith was ever real.” The dragon launched skyward. BOOOOOOM. Wind tore through the garden. Trees shattered. Light bent. And then— They were gone. Nobody spoke immediately. Heavy. Unsettling. The team slowly rose. No one spoke. Because for the first time— They had faced something beyond them. The enemy advanced. Everyone was exhausted. Diago stepped forward alone. Not because he believed he could win. Because teachers stand between danger and students. "Run," he said calmly. Sarko shook his head. "We fight together—" "Not this time." The great bear drew his massive sword. "A teacher's duty..." His eyes never left the enemy. "...is making sure the lesson survives." Sarko stepped forward. Closed his eyes. Steady now. “Divine Restoration.” Golden light spread outward. Deep. Complete. It restored them fully. Body. Spirit. Resolve. Naomi spoke softly: “The Spirit of God sustains us.” Levi nodded. “And through the Son… we stand.” Sarko looked down at his glowing mark. Memories stirred. Faith. Jesus Christ. The moment he first believed. And now— He understood. “This isn’t just power…” He said gently. “It’s purpose.” Levi turned toward the path ahead. “Then we move.” As they left the broken garden— Shadows stirred once more. New enemies. Drawn by their light. But this time— The team stood ready. Together, they covered each other's weaknesses. Stronger. CLASS EVOLUTION AVAILABLE • Guardian Shepherd • Radiant Vanguard • Celestial Ranger • Fortress Titan Levi looked at them all. “This…” He said calmly, “…is only the beginning.”

chapters.title: 13  Breath of Heaven
chapters.summary: Corrupted creatures surge forward. Hailey finds courage and calls down Celestial Rain to shield her friends.
chapters.text: Chapter Thirteen: Breath of Heaven The corrupted creatures surged forward— Twisted animal forms of stone and root, their glowing red eyes filled with rage.
