But this time— The team did not falter Hailey suddenly looked upward. Too many enemies. Too many angles. Levi was trapped. Isaac was down. Sarko's barrier cracked. Everyone turned toward Hailey. The axolotl looked terrified. Her paws trembled around the bow. Then she inhaled slowly. Raised it. One arrow. Two arrows. Twenty. Hundreds. Constellations formed overhead. Her orbiting lights expanded until the sky itself seemed covered in radiant stars. "Celestial Rain." Light crashed downward. The battlefield disappeared beneath falling radiance. Enemies staggered everywhere. Silence followed. Hailey lowered her bow shakily. "I almost didn't shoot." Sarko smiled. "But you did." . Sarko, the lion, stood firm at the center. “Kingdom Sanctuary!” Golden light erupted outward. The battlefield shifted instantly. Waiz, the wolf, became a streak of radiant wind, tearing through enemies before they could react. Amaya, the cheetah, moved like lightning given form—precise, unstoppable. Hailey, the axolotl, climbed onto higher ground as her radiant arrows aligned perfectly above the battlefield. Isaac, the rhino, anchored the ground itself—an unbreakable wall. And Levi, the tiger, moved with flawless control—guiding every moment. The corrupted beasts crashed into them— Again. And again. But nothing broke. Because now— Their strength didn’t come from themselves. It came from trust. From surrender. From God moving through them. Levi’s voice thundered: “Stand firm in faith!” The dove marks ignited across every member. Heaven answered. Golden pillars of light descended. The corrupted beasts froze— Terrified. A voice echoed: “Faithful ones… continue.” BOOOOOOM. Light consumed the battlefield. Every corrupted creature disintegrated instantly. Gone. Silence returned. Not broken. Victorious. The chimes began. CLASS EVOLUTION COMPLETE Sarko stood still, feeling it fully now. Not just power. Calling. Transformation. He was no longer just a Shepherd. He was becoming something greater. Something Heaven was shaping. Days passed. The team journeyed deeper into Chadash Adamah. The world changed around them. Forests gave way to towering cliffs marked with ancient symbols. Rivers of glowing blue light flowed beneath stone bridges older than memory. At night, the stars burned brighter than anything Sarko had ever seen. And the team— Had changed. Waiz moved like living wind itself. Amaya commanded lightning with precision. Hailey’s radiant arrows floated like galaxies above him. Isaac felt less like a warrior— And more like a fortress given life. And Sarko… Sarko could feel the burdens of others now. Not overwhelming. Compassionate. Guided.

chapters.title: 14  The King of Lies
chapters.summary: The road to the king passes through a glowing canyon. Lies and grief challenge what the party believes about strength.
chapters.text: Chapter Fourteen: The King of Lies Levi, the tiger, walked beside Sarko through a canyon glowing with bioluminescent stone. Blue light shimmered across the walls while distant rivers echoed beneath the cliffs. “You’re learning quickly,” Levi said gently. Sarko adjusted the shield across his back. “I still feel like I barely understand any of this.” Levi nodded once. “That feeling never disappears.” Sarko blinked. “Even for you?” Levi’s tail moved calmly behind him as moonlight reflected across his armor. “The closer you grow to God,” he said softly, “the more you realize how infinite He truly is.” The words stayed with Sarko. Naomi stopped walking. The white deer’s glowing eyes narrowed ahead. “Someone approaches.” Instantly the team shifted into formation. Isaac lifted his hammer. Waiz drew both blades. Amaya lowered into a fighting stance. Hailey’s arrow quivers circled faster around her glowing frills. But Levi— Didn’t attack. He stared ahead with visible confusion. A figure stepped from the shadows. Massive. Royal. Terrifying. A white tiger wearing dark crimson armor. Silver stripes shimmered beneath the canyon light. Rex Draconum did not feel like an ordinary enemy. He felt like the embodiment of absolute control—a king who had convinced himself that dependence and vulnerability only led to suffering. Even his calmness felt dangerous. Rex Draconum. But something felt different. No immediate hostility. No crushing aura. Only calm. Too calm. Rex looked across the group slowly. “You’ve grown stronger.” Waiz narrowed his eyes. “That sentence somehow sounded threatening.” Rex ignored him. His golden eyes settled on Sarko. “You carry Heaven’s light unusually well.” Sarko stiffened. Levi stepped slightly forward. “State your purpose.” Rex smiled faintly. “To offer truth.” The canyon fell silent. Naomi’s ears lowered slightly. Something felt wrong. Rex walked slowly toward them. “You fight.” “You suffer.” “You bleed.” “And for what?” His voice echoed unnaturally through the canyon. “To remain servants.” Isaac growled. “Careful.” But Rex continued. “You call yourselves Children of God… yet you chain yourselves willingly.” Dark energy pulsed faintly beneath his armor. “Your light limits you.” Levi’s expression hardened instantly. “Enough.” But Rex raised one claw calmly. “No, Apostle.” “You especially should understand.” His eyes sharpened. “How many souls have you failed to save?” Levi said nothing. Rex stepped closer. “The light gives you rules.” “Boundaries.” “Limits.” His voice lowered. “But I discovered something greater.” Darkness began swirling around one paw— Light around the other. The team froze. Both energies existed together. Impossible. Rex smiled. “Why choose between light and darkness… when both can belong to you?” Sarko felt something twist inside his chest. Temptation. Not loud. Subtle. Rex’s voice became almost gentle. “God fears what you could become.” Levi’s eyes widened slightly. Dangerous. Very dangerous. Rex spread both paws outward. “He tells you surrender is strength because He fears independent power.” Golden and crimson energy spiraled together behind him. “He calls pride evil because He does not want equals.” Naomi whispered softly: “No…” But Rex kept speaking. “You think Heaven made you sons and daughters?” His smile darkened. “No.” “He made pawns.” The canyon trembled. “You heal.” “You protect.” “You sacrifice.” “And still you kneel.” His eyes locked onto Sarko. “But what if you didn’t have to?” Heavy. Sarko felt it. The pull. Because part of him remembered weakness. Pain. Fear. Rex saw it immediately. “Yes…” The Dragon King stepped closer. “You’ve tasted power already.” “And you know it feels good.” Golden light glowed softly around Sarko’s paws. “What if your limits disappeared?” “What if your healing could command life itself?” “What if you no longer served Heaven…” Darkness rose higher. “…but surpassed it?” Waiz swallowed hard. “Okay that’s definitely evil.” But even he looked unsettled. Amaya tightened her grip on her spear. Hailey’s arrow quivers flickered nervously. Rex’s voice thundered now. “I found what Heaven hides.” The canyon cracked beneath him. “A power beyond obedience.” “Beyond submission.” “Beyond God Himself.” Levi stepped forward instantly. “LIES.” BOOOOOOM. Golden light exploded from the Apostle. The canyon shook violently. Levi’s voice thundered with authority. “Creation does not surpass its Creator.” Rex smiled wider. “Then why did Heaven fear knowledge in the beginning?” Silence hit the team. Sarko’s heart pounded. Rex pointed toward the glowing dove mark on Sarko’s paw. “He limits you because He knows what you could become.” Darkness and light twisted violently together around Rex’s body. “You could wield both.” Naomi suddenly cried out: “SARKO DON’T LISTEN!” Too late. For one brief moment— Sarko imagined it. Unlimited strength. No fear. No weakness. No dependence. Power without surrender. And Rex saw the hesitation. His smile widened instantly. “Yes…” “You feel it.” Dark glowing frills of energy erupted behind him as the illusion shattered completely. The canyon exploded under overwhelming pressure. “This is the truth Heaven fears!” Waiz shouted: “THERE IT IS!” Rex’s full power detonated outward. Darkness. Light. Corrupted together. The sky split above the canyon. Isaac slammed his hammer down. “FORMATION TWELVE!” The team moved instantly. But Sarko stood frozen for half a second longer. Because Rex’s words had struck something dangerous. Not hatred toward God. Pride. The desire to become more than created. Levi appeared beside him instantly. “Sarko.” The lion looked up. Levi’s eyes were calm. Steady. “God never feared humanity becoming powerful.” Golden light radiated from the Apostle. “He feared what pride would turn us into.” The words shattered the temptation instantly. Sarko remembered. The journey. The sacrifices. The unity. The grace that carried them. Not domination. Love. Rex roared and charged. The battle exploded across the canyon.

chapters.title: 15  The Fall of the Dragon King
chapters.summary: Rex and his dragon unleash crimson fire. The team stands together against a power that seems impossible to overcome.
chapters.text: Chapter Fifteen: The Fall of the Dragon King Rex Draconum did not feel like an ordinary enemy. He felt like the embodiment of absolute control—a king who had convinced himself that dependence and vulnerability only led to suffering. Even his calmness felt dangerous. The canyon trembled beneath Rex Draconum’s power. Darkness and crimson fire spiraled around the white tiger king as his massive black dragon descended behind him once more. Its scales glowed with molten fractures while smoke poured from its jaws like volcanic breath. The ground cracked. Mountains shook. And for the first time— The team understood they were facing something close to impossible. Rex stood atop a broken cliff, his crimson mantle whipping through the storm winds. “You still cling to weakness,” he said calmly. Golden light and dark energy twisted together around his claws. “You call dependence virtue.” “You call surrender wisdom.” “But power belongs to those willing to rise above limits.” The dragon roared. BOOOOOOOOM. Fire consumed the canyon. “MOVE!” Levi roared. The tiger Apostle exploded forward first, claws igniting with radiant light as he slashed through the flames before they reached the others. “Kingdom Sanctuary!” Sarko slammed his shield into the earth. Golden barriers erupted across the battlefield just as the dragonfire crashed against them. The impact shattered stone for miles. CRACK. The barrier held. Barely. Waiz stared wide-eyed. “THAT was the opening attack?!” Rex vanished. Too fast. CLANG. Levi blocked instantly as Rex appeared directly in front of him, claws colliding with Levi’s radiant blade. Shockwaves exploded through the canyon. Both tigers pushed against each other with terrifying force. Rex smiled slightly. “You improved.” Levi growled. “And you became a slave to power.” Rex’s eyes darkened instantly. BOOM. He blasted Levi backward through multiple stone pillars. “SPLIT FORMATION!” Diago roared. The battlefield erupted into chaos. The dragon descended. Isaac charged first. “FORTRESS TITAN!” Golden runes exploded across the rhino’s armor as he slammed directly into the dragon’s chest. CRAAAAASH. The dragon staggered. But only for a second. Its tail whipped around— BOOM. Isaac was launched through the canyon wall. “TORVAK!” Sarko shouted. Before Sarko could move— Rex appeared above him. Claws descending. SHING. Amaya intercepted instantly, lightning exploding from her spear as she drove Rex backward. “MOVE, SHEPHERD!” Sarko rolled aside just as dark energy obliterated the ground beneath him. Hailey climbed onto a high stone ridge overlooking the battlefield. The female axolotl drew her radiant bow. Her glowing frills pulsed brightly. Eyes focused. Calm. “Celestial Volley.” FWIP. FWIP. FWIP. Three radiant arrows streaked across the battlefield at impossible angles. One struck the dragon’s eye. Another pierced the joints beneath its wing. The third exploded against Rex’s shoulder. Rex looked upward. Interested. Hailey drew another arrow instantly. “More than that.” She released again. This time the arrows multiplied mid-flight— splitting into dozens of radiant projectiles raining across the battlefield like falling stars. The dragon roared as explosions erupted across its scales. Waiz grinned wildly. “NOW WE’RE TALKING!” The gray wolf accelerated like living wind itself. He sprinted up falling debris— leapt— and slashed across the dragon’s neck repeatedly. SLASH. SLASH. SLASH. The dragon snapped toward him— Too late. Amaya struck next. “THUNDER BREAKER!” Lightning detonated across the dragon’s skull. BOOOOM. The canyon lit white. But Rex moved again. CRASH. Waiz was blasted from the sky. Amaya barely blocked Rex’s claws before being driven backward across the battlefield. Levi re-entered instantly. CLANG. Tiger against tiger. Light against corrupted power. Their battle alone shook the canyon apart. Sarko saw it— Rex wasn’t just stronger. He was combining both light and darkness together. Unstable. Violent. But powerful. And every second he used it— The corruption inside him spread further. Naomi’s eyes widened. “His body is breaking apart…” Diago growled. “He’s consuming himself.” The dragon opened its jaws. A massive sphere of crimson-black fire formed inside its throat. The entire canyon began collapsing from the pressure alone. Hailey’s eyes widened. “That blast will destroy everything.” Levi shouted instantly: “EVERYONE TOGETHER!” The team moved as one. Isaac planted himself at the front. Sarko beside him. Levi directly behind them. Waiz and Amaya on the flanks. Hailey and Naomi in the rear. Rex smiled coldly. “Yes. Stand together, so you may fall together.” The dragon fired. BOOOOOOOOOOOOM. The beam erased the canyon. Mountains vaporized. The earth split open. And the team— Held. Barely. Sarko screamed as Kingdom Sanctuary cracked around them. Golden light splintered. Isaac’s legs buckled. Waiz collapsed to one knee. Amaya staggered as the barrier cracked around her. Hailey’s bow shattered apart in her paws. CRACK. The dragonfire pierced through. Sarko’s eyes widened. It struck Hailey directly. BOOOOOOM. The axolotl was thrown violently across the battlefield. “HAILEY!” Naomi screamed. She crashed against broken stone. Sarko felt it through Shared Burden. Pain. Unimaginable pain. He turned— And froze. Hailey’s left arm was gone. Burned away completely. Waiz stared in horror. “No…” Even Rex paused. Hailey trembled violently—trying to stand despite the injury. But instead of fear— She reached for another arrow. Levi’s eyes widened slightly. Still fighting. Sarko ran toward her instantly. “DIVINE RESTORATION!” Golden light exploded around them. The battlefield stopped. Radiant energy wrapped around Hailey’s body. Bone formed. Muscle returned. Soft axolotl skin regenerated. Her glowing frills reignited. Slowly— Her arm regrew completely. Everyone stared. Even Rex. Hailey flexed her restored arm slowly—then calmly picked up another bow from the rubble. “…that was unpleasant.” Waiz burst out laughing in disbelief. “SHE SAID IT SO CALMLY.” Rex stared at Sarko now. Not amused anymore. Concerned. “You restored what was completely destroyed…” Sarko shook his head with a small smile. “I supported her, but the regeneration was part of how the Creator made her.” Golden light radiated across the battlefield. “Love restores what power destroys.” The words hit Rex harder than any attack. His composure cracked. Rage exploded outward. “ENOUGH!” Darkness erupted from his body violently. The dragon roared with him. The final battle began. Levi moved first. “NOW!” Everything aligned. Isaac locked down the dragon’s movement. Amaya overloaded its nervous system with lightning strikes. Waiz severed tendons across its legs. Hailey fired precision arrows directly into weak points exposed by Radiant Mark. Naomi guided every movement through prophetic foresight. Diago shattered the dragon’s armor apart piece by piece. And Sarko— Connected all of them. Shared Burden ignited brighter than ever before. Every heartbeat synchronized. Every movement amplified. Every soul united. Rex attacked Levi with overwhelming fury— But Levi no longer fought alone. CLANG. CLANG. CLANG. Every strike Rex made— someone countered. Every opening— someone covered. The dragon rose into the air— Hailey fired upward instantly. “HEARTSEEKER!” A radiant arrow pierced directly through the dragon’s chest. BOOOOOOM. The dragon crashed from the sky. Rex’s eyes widened. “No…” Isaac seized the opening. “FORTRESS DESCENT!” The rhino slammed Rex into the canyon floor. Amaya struck next. Waiz followed. Diago shattered Rex’s defenses. Levi crossed both glowing claws before him. “Radiant Judgment.” SHING. A massive cross-shaped wave of light tore through the battlefield. Rex staggered backward. Armor shattered. Darkness unstable. Then Sarko stepped forward. Not with rage. With compassion. “Divine Restoration.” Light exploded directly into Rex’s core. Visions erupted around him. Loneliness. Pride. Pain. Isolation. The desperate need to become greater because he feared weakness. And beneath it all— Fear of surrender. Rex dropped to one knee. His claws trembled. The dragon behind him dissolved into ash and fading embers. Quiet settled over the canyon. The Dragon King— defeated. Barely standing. Broken armor hung from his body. Blood dripped across shattered stone. And for the first time— Rex Draconum did not feel like an ordinary enemy. He felt like the embodiment of absolute control—a king who had convinced himself that dependence and vulnerability only led to suffering. Even his calmness felt dangerous. Rex Draconum looked tired. Not angry. Not prideful. Just… exhausted. Levi approached slowly. The tiger Apostle stood over him gently. Rex laughed weakly. “…so this is what unity looks like.” Levi answered calmly: “No.” Golden light reflected across the ruined battlefield. “This is what love looks like.” As the last echoes of battle faded, Sarko thought again of the lion he had been in the flood—afraid, frozen, convinced that one terrible moment defined him. Now he understood. Courage was not never being afraid. Faithfulness was not guaranteeing that nobody would ever be hurt. A Shepherd was called to love, protect, and obey—and to trust God with what remained beyond his reach.

chapters.title: 16  The City of Light
chapters.summary: After the battle, corruption breaks open in Rex. The party reaches the City of Light and sees a path toward healing.
chapters.text: Chapter Sixteen: The City of Light Quiet settled over the canyon—not the silence of fear, but the deep stillness that comes after a storm has finally ended. At the center of the shattered battlefield stood Rex Draconum, the white tiger. Golden light spread slowly through the fractures in his dark armor as the last traces of corruption dissolved from his body. The darkness was gone. Not forced away, but broken open from within. Rex looked down at his trembling paws as though seeing them clearly for the first time in centuries. His breathing shook unevenly. Blood mixed with tears along his face. “All this time…” he whispered. “I thought strength meant never needing anyone.” Levi stepped forward calmly, his crimson mantle shifting softly in the wind. “And where did that road lead you?” For a long moment, Rex said nothing. His eyes drifted toward the team standing together nearby—the wolf, the cheetah, the axolotl, the rhino, the deer, and Sarko himself. Bruised. Exhausted. Barely able to stand. Yet still together. A faint smile touched Rex’s face for the first time, free from bitterness or pride. “Alone.” The crimson glow faded completely from his eyes. Dark energy dissolved into harmless streams of light that drifted upward like dying embers into the sky. The crushing pressure over the canyon vanished. The fear vanished with it. Only peace remained. Waiz finally broke the silence. “So…” the gray wolf said carefully, gesturing toward the completely destroyed battlefield around them, “…does this count as a team-building exercise?” Amaya let out a long breath. “Yes.” Isaac burst into booming laughter. “BEST TEAM BUILDING!” Hailey collapsed backward onto a rock, her glowing frills drooping dramatically. “I almost died seven times.” Waiz grinned. “Only seven? That’s improvement.” For the first time in what felt like forever, the team laughed together. No enemies remained. No fear lingered. Only relief. Sarko looked around at them gently. His team. His family. Not because they were perfect, but because they had chosen one another through every trial, every wound, and every moment of darkness. Then Levi turned toward the horizon. Everyone followed his gaze. And there— Waiz blinked slowly. “…I don’t even think I need sleep anymore.” Hailey stared ahead in awe. “Do you realize how much time that adds to existence?” “MORE ADVENTURE,” Isaac declared proudly. Naomi smiled softly beside them. “We’re close.” Then they saw it. The Heavenly City ahead of them. Sarko forgot how to breathe. No kingdom in existence could compare to what stood before them. Massive walls of radiant gold shimmered like living light beneath the endless sky. Rivers brighter than crystal flowed through its streets, while trees bearing glowing fruit lined the pathways beyond the gates. Music filled the air—not played by instruments, but alive somehow, woven into the atmosphere itself. And at the center of the city burned a light brighter than the sun. Yet it was not harsh. It was gentle. Beautiful. Perfect. Waiz stared speechless before finally whispering, “…how do you even describe that?” Levi smiled faintly. “You don’t.” The light of the Heavenly City burned brighter than ever before. No longer distant. Close. They walked together into the final valley. The world changed around them. Rivers shimmered like crystal. Trees glowed with gentle life. The air itself carried peace. And as they walked— Something shifted. Their exhaustion disappeared. Completely. No hunger. No pain. No fear. Only fullness. The gates stood open before them, towering high above like the entrance to eternity itself. Beside them stood radiant beings clothed in white light. Angels. Their eyes rested upon the glowing dove marks carried by each member of the team—not broken now, but whole. Restored. One angel stepped forward, its voice carrying warmth and authority like music wrapped in thunder. “The King has awaited your arrival.” Then the gates opened fully. Light poured outward like the dawn of creation itself. Sarko stepped forward first. The moment he crossed into the city, everything changed. Every trace of weakness disappeared. Every fear dissolved. Every wound carried from his past—every failure, every insecurity, every hidden ache buried deep within him—was suddenly gone. Not hidden. Healed. He did not become someone different. He became who he had always been meant to be. Around him, the others felt it too. Isaac fell to his knees openly weeping. Hailey laughed and cried at the same time, overwhelmed by joy she could barely contain. Amaya covered her face as silent tears slipped through trembling paws. And Waiz simply whispered one quiet word. “…home.” Together, they walked deeper into the city toward the great light at its center. The closer they came, the stronger its presence became. Not merely emotion. Presence. Living. Waiting. Then they saw Him. Jesus. Sarko froze completely. No description could possibly contain Him. Light radiated gently from Him, and yet everything in creation seemed to revolve around His presence. His eyes carried endless kindness and absolute authority at the same time. The scars in His hands remained, but now they shone with glory brighter than the stars themselves. Jesus looked at Sarko with a kindness that seemed to reach all the way back to the storm. “I saw you in the rain,” He said. Sarko’s throat tightened. “I thought I had to make up for it.” “You were never asked to become everyone’s savior,” Jesus replied. “You were called to follow Me faithfully.” Sarko looked down at the shield that had carried him across Chadash Adamah. At last, the old weight inside him loosened. “I can protect them,” Sarko whispered. “I can love them. But I am not their Savior.” Jesus smiled. “Now you understand the heart of a Shepherd.” And when He smiled— Sarko felt more loved than he had ever believed possible. Not because he had earned it. Not because he had achieved greatness. Simply because he was His. The entire team fell to their knees instinctively, overwhelmed by the holiness before them. But Jesus stepped forward immediately. “No,” He said softly, His voice carrying warmth deeper than existence itself. “You are home now.” He reached down and lifted Sarko to his feet first, then embraced him. And in that moment, every longing Sarko had ever carried vanished completely. Every question faded away. Not because he suddenly understood everything, but because he was finally with the One he had been searching for his entire life. Jesus looked toward the rest of the team with gentle pride shining in His eyes. “Well done.” Then another presence approached. Greater. Infinite. Holy. The Father. No fear remained within any of them now. Only belonging. The Father opened His arms, and instantly the entire team ran forward like children finally returning home after wandering for far too long. He embraced them fully. Completely. And within His presence, nothing was missing anymore. No striving. No pain. No loneliness. Only joy. Perfect joy.

chapters.title: 17  The Undying Earth
chapters.summary: At the Heavenly City, Sarko and his friends finally rest. Their journey has changed them, and the light continues beyond them.
chapters.text: Chapter Seventeen: The Undying Earth For the first time since Sarko awakened in Chadash Adamah, there was no danger. No rushing. No battle waiting beyond the horizon. Only quiet. The team stood together near the gates of the Heavenly City while countless lights moved across distant roads below. Travelers. Pilgrims. Children of God still journeying home. Sarko quietly looked at his friends. Isaac rested against his hammer while Amaya stood nearby, finally allowing herself to relax. Hailey watched glowing birds circle above the walls while Naomi smiled softly at everything around them. Diago crossed his arms as always. Levi simply stood still. For once, the Apostle looked peaceful. Sarko looked beyond the City walls. Mountains stretched endlessly. Kingdoms covered valleys. Forests rolled across the horizon beneath golden light. The Undying Earth. It felt strange. Their entire journey had been about reaching the City. Now they were here. “What happens now?” Sarko asked quietly. Jesus stood beside them overlooking creation itself. “Now comes responsibility.” The team listened carefully. “This world has been restored, but restoration must now spread. For one thousand years, you who carry My mark will reign with Me.” Isaac blinked. “Reign how?” Jesus smiled gently. “Not through domination. Through service.” He pointed toward the kingdoms below. “You will establish justice. You will protect the weak. You will rebuild what corruption damaged. You will teach those still learning truth. You will help guide nations. And where monsters remain—you will remove them.” The team stood silently. The mission was larger than they imagined. Jesus continued. “Every one of you was shaped for this.” His eyes moved across them. “Isaac, you will help establish strongholds of protection.” The rhino grinned proudly. “Shield brother approves.” “Amaya, you will help train defenders.” She nodded once. “Understood.” “Hailey, you will help restore communities.” Her glowing frills lifted happily. “I’d like that.” “Naomi, you will help guide those who cannot yet see clearly.” Naomi lowered her head gently. “I will.” “Waiz.” The wolf blinked nervously. “Uh oh.” Jesus smiled. “You will encourage those who are losing hope.” Waiz went quiet for a moment before smiling. “Yeah. I can do that.” “Diago, you will raise new protectors.” The great bear nodded once. “As always.” Then Jesus looked toward Levi. “Apostle.” Levi lowered his head. “You will help lead.” Finally, Jesus looked toward Sarko. “Shepherd.” Sarko straightened. “Your role remains unchanged.” Sarko blinked. “Protect people?” Jesus smiled warmly. “Bring them together.” Something settled deeply inside Sarko. Not stronger. Clearer. Far below the City, lights moved endlessly across distant roads. Thousands. Then more. Children of God still journeying home. Sarko stared. “There are that many?” Jesus smiled. “Far more.” Massive doors opened behind them. An angel stepped forward. Radiant chains surrounded a familiar prisoner. Rex Draconum. The white tiger no longer carried his crown. No armor. No dragon. Only silence. The angel bowed. “The prisoner awaits confinement.” Jesus nodded. “For one thousand years.” Rex looked once toward Levi. Then Sarko. Regret filled his eyes. Then light surrounded him. Gone. Silence followed. Then distant trumpets echoed. Jesus smiled softly. “More children are arriving.” The team turned. Far beyond the gates another group approached. Six figures. Battle-worn. Victorious. Different. Leading them was a towering mountain goat covered in climbing gear and crystal-edged weapons strapped across his back. Beside him walked a river otter surrounded by floating tools and strange glowing inventions. A snowy owl glided overhead wrapped in silver armor while a scarred water buffalo carried scripture-covered armor across broad shoulders. A red panda struggled beneath an oversized glowing book. Then Levi froze. Walking quietly behind them was a tiger. Older. Scarred. Ancient Apostle markings covered worn armor. One eye crossed by an old scar. His dove mark glowed brightly. “…Cassiel?” The tiger stopped. Then slowly smiled. “Well…” His voice cracked slightly. “Took you long enough.” Waiz blinked. “You know this guy?” Cassiel laughed softly. “We survived training together.” Levi stepped forward slowly. “You disappeared.” Cassiel nodded. “Our road went west.” His eyes moved across Sarko’s team. “And yours clearly became complicated.” Isaac whispered loudly. “Tiger knows other tiger.” For the first time since meeting him, Levi looked emotional. Jesus looked toward the endless roads beyond the City. More lights appeared. Then more. Then countless more. His voice remained gentle. “The work begins now.” Sarko looked at his team. His family. Their journey toward the City was over. But their purpose had only just begun. To Be Continued…
